Founder & Lead Instructor

Built and Taught by Lakshmi Ma'am

Laxmi Fashion Design Academy was founded by Lakshmi ma'am, and every class is still led personally by her — no handoffs to junior staff, no generic video lessons. You learn the way tailoring has always been taught: side by side, needle in hand, one technique at a time.

It shows in the reviews. Students describe her as one of the finest in the field — patient with complete beginners, thorough on advanced techniques, and known for a teaching style that's friendly, comfortable and easy to follow, whether you're cutting your first pattern or finishing bridal-level zardosi work.

Full Course

6 Months

Everything in one program — the complete path from your very first stitch to bridal-level aari embroidery, without pausing between packages to enroll again.

  • Covers all seven tracks below, taught in sequence
  • Basic sewing → blouse-making → dress & gown design → aari embroidery
  • Best value if you're starting from zero and want the full skill set
  • The path several of our students — including long-time reviewers — have completed

Basic Course

15 Days

Start from zero. Get comfortable on every machine and tool, learn hand and machine stitches, and finish nine small projects of your own.

  • Machine & tool orientation, all stitching machines
  • Hand-sewing methods & cutting techniques
  • Needle techniques & pattern-making basics
  • 9 beginner projects — tote bag, pouches, apron & more

Day by Day

  1. D1Machine introduction
  2. D2Tools introduction
  3. D3Operating all types of tailoring machines
  4. D4Practice stitches
  5. D5Hand sewing methods
  6. D6Cutting techniques
  7. D7Basic to advanced cutting machines
  8. D8Pressure foot types & uses
  9. D9All kinds of needle techniques
  10. D10Pattern-making method
  11. D11Beginner project list

Projects: tote bag, pin cushion, pillow covers, zip pouch, reversible hand bag, travel bag with zip, apron, saree fall corner stitching, and zip/hook/eye/button stitching.

Basic Blouse Package

1 Month

Learn to take a customer's measurements, draft a pattern, and stitch a complete blouse from scratch — fully hands-on.

  • Measurement-taking & pattern calculation
  • Cloth handling, marking & cutting
  • Brazier-cut & princess-cut blouses
  • Neck design, sleeve styles & piping methods

What You'll Learn

  1. 1Taking measurements from the customer
  2. 2Calculating measurements for a blouse pattern
  3. 3Cloth handling method
  4. 4Placing patterns on cloth
  5. 5Cloth marking
  6. 6Cloth cutting
  7. 7Detailed blouse stitching — completely hands-on

Covers: brazier-cut blouse, princess-cut blouse (1 & 2), katori-work blouse, 5 sleeve designs, neck design methods, piping methods, hangings, and embroidery/aari marking methods.

Curriculum Depth

What's Included

Tools & Materials You'll Work With

Training includes hands-on access to a full range of tailoring and aari embroidery equipment, so you focus on learning the technique, not sourcing the tools.

Threads & Yarns

Anchor threads, silk threads, jari (gold) threads, heavy cotton thread and piping thread.

Aari & Embroidery Tools

Aari stand, aari cot, all kinds of needles, and a punch machine for design transfer.

Fabric & Marking

Cotton cloth, silk-cotton cloth, net cloth, cloth marker, chalk powder and tracing sheets.

Cutting & Finishing

Small scissor, cross scissor, stitch remover, fabric glue, naada roll and an electric heating machine.

Paper & Planning

A4 sheets, pens and pencils for design markings and pattern notes.

Aari Design Kits

Basic aari material sets (25 packages) for hands-on practice on real design markings.
